The clinical presentation centers on acute-to-subacute gait and limb ataxia with *asymmetric right upper limb weakness* — a key nuance. While classic cerebellar ataxia is typically symmetric and non-paretic, the presence of *subjective right upper limb weakness* (even if not yet confirmed objectively) introduces a critical red flag: it suggests possible involvement beyond the cerebellum — e.g., corticospinal tract, brainstem, or cerebellar peduncle pathology. - It fits the tempo (subacute),  
- Explains ataxia without mandatory dysarthria/nystagmus (variant presentations exist),  
- Is compatible with asymmetric onset (reported in anti-GAD65 and anti-mGluR1 cases),
